description: Reference/untreated group of the study's main comparison (no treatment or stress applied; time-matched where the study is a time course).
Exposed to the study's main treatment/perturbation (chemical, physical or nutritional shift). Pair with the tag naming the treatment itself.
Sampled from a culture that will be treated, but before the treatment/shift started (pre-treatment reference point).
No intended genetic modification relative to the study's parental strain (includes the study's own 'WT' control strain).
Carries at least one gene deletion/disruption. Pair with del_<gene> or a phenotype-level tag naming what was removed.
Carries a construct overexpressing an endogenous gene. Pair with oe_<gene>.
Expresses a gene from another organism.
alpha-1,3-glucan synthase gene(s) deleted (cell-wall polysaccharide; deletion reduces hyphal aggregation).
Galactosaminogalactan (GAG) synthesis gene(s) deleted (deletion reduces hyphal aggregation).
Engineered to grow as dispersed hyphae instead of pellets/aggregates in liquid culture.
Strain used in industrial/food production (e.g. koji starter), as opposed to a laboratory reference strain.
Liquid (submerged) culture of any kind: shake flask, tube or bioreactor.
Solid-state fermentation on a moist particulate substrate (e.g. koji on steamed soybean/wheat). Not agar plates -- see surface_culture.
Growth on the surface of agar (optionally over cellophane) or of a soaked support; some authors call this 'solid culture'.
Shaken flask culture.
Controlled stirred-tank (or similar) bioreactor culture.
Fed-batch operation (nutrient feed during cultivation).
Chemically defined medium (includes minimal media such as Czapek-Dox).
Medium containing undefined natural components (peptone, yeast extract, potato infusion, ...).
Czapek-Dox (CD/CZ) minimal medium or a modification of it.
Potato dextrose broth or agar (PDB/PDA).
Maltose-peptone-yeast extract (MPY) medium.
Glucose is a supplied carbon source (sole or co-substrate).
Maltose is the supplied carbon source.
Fructose is the supplied carbon source.
Lactate/lactic acid is a supplied carbon source.
Two or more carbon sources supplied together.
Main carbon source is non-fermentable (e.g. lactate, acetate, glycerol).
Carbon supply limiting growth, or the supplied carbon source(s) reported as exhausted at sampling time.
Nitrate (e.g. NaNO3) is the nitrogen source.
Urea is a nitrogen source.
Nitrogen supplied as peptone/yeast extract/protein-rich material.
Steamed soybean (or soybean-based material) as growth substrate.
Wheat flour or wheat bran as growth substrate.
Koji (mold-fermented substrate) production.
Context of soy sauce brewing.
DTT (reducing agent) added; classic inducer of ER stress.
Furfural added (furan aldehyde, lignocellulosic-hydrolysate inhibitor).
Triton X-100 (non-ionic surfactant) in the medium.
A surfactant/detergent is present in the medium.
Endoplasmic reticulum (protein-folding) stress induced by the treatment.
Exposure to a growth-inhibitory chemical (toxin, inhibitor, xenobiotic).
Exposure to a by-product of lignocellulose pretreatment (furfural, HMF, vanillin, ferulic/levulinic acid, ...).
Low oxygen availability (e.g. dissolved oxygen <= 1%).
Oxygen supply maintained (not oxygen-limited) in a study that manipulates oxygen.
Active (exponential / mid-log) growth at sampling.
Growth has ceased / stationary phase at sampling.
Sampled material is vegetative mycelium (hyphae).
Resting (dormant, ungerminated) conidia.
Conidia incubated under germination-permissive conditions (before/at germ-tube emergence).
Culture sampled during conidiation/sporulation.
Ammonium (e.g. (NH4)2SO4) is the nitrogen source.
